# Build system: design

## Data structures

The build system's "data structures" are make variables. The ones with
cross-file meaning:

| Variable | Set in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ROOT` | `Makefile` | absolute path of the tree; every source path is `$(ROOT)/...` |
| `ARCH`, `BUILD`, `OUT`, `V`, `SELFTEST`, `CRASH_TEST`, `QEMU_*`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, `BUILD_ID` | `build/config.mk` | user-facing knobs and derived identity |
| `CC`, `LD`, `LDLINK`, `OBJCOPY`, `NM`, `OBJDUMP`, `PYTHON`, `LLVM_PREFIX` | `build/toolchain.mk` | tool names |
| `KERNEL_TARGET`, `LOADER_TARGET`, `KERNEL_ARCH_CFLAGS`, `KERNEL_ARCH_LDFLAGS`, `LOADER_ARCH_CFLAGS`, `QEMU_SYSTEM` | `build/arch/<ARCH>.mk` | per-architecture triples and flags |
| `COMMON_WARNINGS`, `COMMON_CFLAGS`, `KERNEL_CFLAGS`, `KERNEL_LDFLAGS`, `LOADER_CFLAGS`, `LOADER_LDFLAGS` | `build/toolchain.mk` | flag sets |
| `KERNEL_GENERIC_SRCS`, `KERNEL_ARCH_SRCS`, `KERNEL_OBJS`, `KERNEL_ELF`, `KERNEL_MAP`, `KERNEL_LINKER_SCRIPT`, `KERNEL_ANALYZE` | `kernel/kernel.mk`, `kernel/arch/<ARCH>/arch.mk` | kernel component |
| `LOADER_SRCS`, `LOADER_OBJS`, `LOADER_EFI`, `LOADER_ANALYZE` | `boot/uefi/boot.mk` | loader component |
| `IMAGE` | `Makefile` | the FAT image |
| `EXTRA_CFLAGS` | target-specific in `kernel/kernel.mk` | per-object additions (the arch include path) |

`build/rules.mk` provides three functions: `objs_of` (sources relative to
`$(ROOT)` to objects under `$(OUT)`), `compile_rules` (static pattern
rules for `.c` plus matching `.analyzed` stamp rules), and
`assemble_rules` (for `.S`). Each component calls them once with its
object list and the name of its CFLAGS variable.

## Ownership and lifetime of outputs

`$(OUT)` is owned entirely by the build and is deleted by `make clean`.
Nothing under it is ever committed (`.gitignore` excludes `out/`). Sibling
trees created by other targets (`$(OUT)-crash` by `test-crash`,
`out/repro-a` and `out/repro-b` by `reproducible`) follow the same rule.
Source directories are never written to.

Dependency files (`*.d`) are generated by `-MMD -MP` and included with
`-include`, so header changes rebuild the right objects and a deleted
header does not break the build.

## Toolchain and flags

### Targets

| Component | Triple | Object format | ABI |
|---|---|---|---|
| kernel | `x86_64-unknown-none-elf` | ELF64 | System V |
| UEFI loader | `x86_64-unknown-windows` | PE/COFF | Microsoft x64 (what UEFI requires) |

Using the Windows triple for the loader is what makes `efi_main` and every
firmware callback use the right calling convention without decorating
each function. `EFIAPI` in `boot/uefi/efi.h` is kept for readability.

### Shared flags (`COMMON_CFLAGS`)

| Flag | Reason |
|---|---|
| `-std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib` | constitution section 51; no hosted environment |
| `-nostdinc` plus `-isystem $(clang -print-resource-dir)/include` | only clang's own `stdint.h`, `stddef.h`, `stdbool.h`, `stdarg.h` are visible; no host headers can leak into target code |
| `-fno-stack-protector` | there is no canary support code yet |
| `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` | `arch_backtrace()` walks frame pointers |
| `-fno-strict-aliasing` | conservative; hardware structures are accessed through casts |
| `-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-unwind-tables` | no unwinder; frame pointers suffice |
| `-ffile-prefix-map=$(ROOT)=/cosmo` | absolute paths do not reach `__FILE__` or DWARF, so builds from different checkouts match |
| `-DCOSMO_BUILD_ID`, `-DCOSMO_BUILD_TYPE`, `-DCONFIG_*` | identity and configuration |
| `-O1 -g -DCONFIG_DEBUG=1` (debug) / `-O2 -g -DCONFIG_DEBUG=0` (release) | `-O0` produces unbounded stack frames; `-O1` keeps debugging usable |

### Warnings (`COMMON_WARNINGS`)

`-Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wvla -Wundef -Wpointer-arith
-Wwrite-strings -Wstrict-prototypes -Wmissing-prototypes
-Wmissing-declarations -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wcast-qual -Wformat=2
-Wdate-time`. `-Wmissing-prototypes` is what forces every non-static
function to have a header declaration. `-Wformat=2` includes
`-Wformat-nonliteral`, so every function that forwards a format string
carries `__printf(n, 0)`. `-Wdate-time` makes `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` an
error, protecting reproducibility.

### Kernel-only flags (`KERNEL_ARCH_CFLAGS`, `KERNEL_LDFLAGS`)

| Flag | Reason |
|---|---|
| `-mcmodel=kernel` | image linked in the top 2 GiB (`0xFFFFFFFF80000000`); sign-extended 32-bit displacements reach everything |
| `-mno-red-zone` | interrupts run on the interrupted stack; the red zone would be clobbered |
| `-mgeneral-regs-only` | no SSE/x87 in the kernel, so traps and context switches never save FP state |
| `-fno-pic -fno-pie` | fixed link address; no dynamic relocation |
| `-nostdlib -static --no-dynamic-linker` | freestanding link |
| `-z max-page-size=0x1000` | segments aligned to 4 KiB, not 2 MiB, so the file stays small and the loader's page-granular mapping applies |
| `-z noexecstack -z separate-code` | no executable stack marker; code and data in separate segments |
| `--build-id=sha1` | deterministic identity note in PT_NOTE |
| `--gc-sections` | drop unreferenced sections; `KEEP()` in `linker.ld` protects entry and notes |

### Loader-only flags (`LOADER_ARCH_CFLAGS`, `LOADER_LDFLAGS`)

| Flag | Reason |
|---|---|
| `-fshort-wchar` | `CHAR16` literals (`L"..."`) must be 16-bit for UEFI |
| `-mno-red-zone -mgeneral-regs-only` | same reasoning as the kernel; firmware callbacks may interrupt |
| `-mno-stack-arg-probe` | clang would otherwise emit `__chkstk` calls for large frames; there is no CRT |
| `/subsystem:efi_application /entry:efi_main /nodefaultlib` | PE header and entry for firmware |
| `/Brepro /timestamp:0` | deterministic PE (no link timestamp, reproducible checksum) |

## Invariant 1 enforcement

`kernel/kernel.mk` splits objects into `KERNEL_GENERIC_OBJS` and
`KERNEL_ARCH_OBJS`. Both compile with `KERNEL_CFLAGS`, which contains only
`-I$(ROOT)/kernel/include -I$(ROOT)/boot/protocol`. The arch objects (and
their analyzer stamps) get a target-specific
`EXTRA_CFLAGS := -I$(ROOT)/kernel/arch/$(ARCH)/include`. A generic file
that writes `#include <x86/cpu.h>` fails to compile. This is the whole
mechanism; there is no lint pass to bypass.

## Concurrency

`make -j` is safe: every rule creates its own output directory with
`mkdir -p` and no two rules write the same file. `test-crash` and
`reproducible` recurse into `make` with distinct `OUT` values. Running
different `BUILD` configurations concurrently in one tree is safe for
the same reason.

## Error handling

- Any compiler warning is an error.
- `scripts/check-kernel-elf.sh` runs as part of the kernel link rule and
  fails the build if a PT_LOAD is writable and executable or PT_NOTE is
  missing, so a linker-script regression is caught before QEMU.
- `scripts/check-tools.sh` reports every missing prerequisite in one run
  rather than stopping at the first.
- Scripts use `set -eu`; the boot test harness reports every failing
  criterion and echoes the whole serial log on failure.
- `build/config.mk` rejects a `BUILD` value other than `debug`/`release`
  with `$(error)`.

## Performance

The full debug build (28 objects, two links, image) takes a few seconds on
either host. Nothing is cached beyond make's timestamps; ccache is not
wired in and is not needed at this size.

## Security

The build is the first place supply-chain risk appears. Currently:
apt/Homebrew-provided toolchains, no downloaded binaries, no network
access during `make`. Reproducible output means an independent build can
verify a published binary. Signing of the loader (for Secure Boot) and of
kernel modules is future work and will be a separate `sign` step, not a
side effect of `all`.

## Future extensibility

- **AArch64**: add `build/arch/aarch64.mk` (`KERNEL_TARGET :=
  aarch64-unknown-none-elf`, `LOADER_TARGET := aarch64-unknown-windows`,
  no code-model flag) and `kernel/arch/aarch64/arch.mk`; `make
  ARCH=aarch64` then works without touching shared files. `qemu-run.sh`
  needs a per-arch machine description.
- **Host tools, libc, userland**: separate component makefiles with their
  own toolchain variables (`HOST_CC` for tools, the target triple plus a
  sysroot for userland). `COMMON_CFLAGS` is kernel/loader-specific and
  must not be reused for hosted code.
- **Sanitizers** (constitution section 49): UBSan in the kernel is a flag
  addition plus a runtime; ASan-like host testing arrives with the host
  unit-test harness.
- **LTO and coverage**: both are flag-level additions on top of the
  existing structure.
